title: Custom & MCP integrations
content:
## Overview

Wingman can be extended with both **first-party** and **custom third-party** Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, giving your agents access to external tools, data sources, and APIs. You configure servers by adding an endpoint and a JSON configuration block; Wingman handles authentication and credential injection at runtime.

<Note>
MCP integrations are managed per workspace. Each server you add becomes available to all agents in that workspace.
</Note>

---

## Supported server types

Emergent currently supports MCP servers that expose:

- **Tools** — callable functions that agents can invoke during conversations (e.g., database queries, file operations, API calls).
- **Resources** — read-only data sources that agents can reference (e.g., documentation, schemas, knowledge bases).

<Warning title="Unsupported: Prompts">
MCP *prompt* primitives are **not yet supported**. Servers that rely exclusively on prompts will not function correctly.
</Warning>

---

## Adding an MCP server

<Steps>

<Step title="Navigate to Wingman settings">
Open the **Wingman** tab in your workspace sidebar, then click the **gear icon** (⚙️) in the top-right corner to open Wingman settings.
</Step>

<Step title="Locate the MCP Servers section">
Scroll to the **Custom & MCP integrations** section. You'll see a list of configured servers (if any) and an **Add Server** button.
</Step>

<Step title="Click Add Server">
Click **Add Server**. A modal will appear prompting you for two fields:

- **Endpoint** — the URL or command that starts the MCP server (see [Endpoint formats](#endpoint-formats) below).
- **Configuration JSON** — a JSON object defining environment variables, arguments, and other server-specific settings.
</Step>

<Step title="Enter the endpoint">
Paste the server's endpoint. Common formats:

- `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres`
- `uvx mcp-server-git`
- `docker run --rm -i your-org/mcp-server:latest`
- `https://your-api.com/mcp` (for HTTP-based servers)

See [Endpoint formats](#endpoint-formats) for details.
</Step>

<Step title="Provide the configuration JSON">
Enter a JSON object with any required environment variables, command-line arguments, or runtime settings. For example:

```json
{
  "env": {
    "DATABASE_URL": "postgresql://user:pass@host:5432/db",
    "API_KEY": "sk-..."
  },
  "args": ["--verbose"]
}
```

Credentials are stored securely and injected at runtime—they are **never logged or exposed** to the agent's conversation history.
</Step>

<Step title="Save and test">
Click **Save**. Wingman will attempt to initialize the server. If successful, you'll see a green checkmark and the server's tools/resources will appear in the Wingman interface. If initialization fails, review the error message and check your endpoint and configuration.
</Step>

</Steps>

---

## Endpoint formats

MCP servers can be invoked in several ways:

| Format | Example | When to use |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| **npx** | `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres` | Official or npm-published MCP servers |
| **uvx** | `uvx mcp-server-git` | Python-based MCP servers using uv |
| **Docker** | `docker run --rm -i your-org/mcp-server:latest` | Containerized servers requiring isolation |
| **HTTP** | `https://your-api.com/mcp` | Remote MCP servers accessible over HTTPS |
| **Local binary** | `/path/to/my-mcp-server` | Custom-built executables |

<Info>
For `npx` and `uvx`, the `-y` flag (or equivalent) auto-accepts prompts. For Docker, `--rm -i` ensures the container is cleaned up and accepts stdin.
</Info>

---

## Configuration JSON schema

The configuration object supports the following keys:

```json
{
  "env": {
    "KEY": "value"
  },
  "args": ["--flag", "value"],
  "timeout": 30000
}
```

- **`env`** *(object, optional)* — Environment variables passed to the server process. Use this for API keys, database URLs, and other secrets.
- **`args`** *(array, optional)* — Command-line arguments appended to the endpoint invocation.
- **`timeout`** *(integer, optional)* — Maximum time in milliseconds to wait for server initialization (default: `30000`).

<Warning title="Credential security">
Secrets in the `env` object are encrypted at rest and injected only when the server is spawned. **Never commit credentials to version control.**
</Warning>

---

## Credential handling

Emergent stores MCP server credentials separately from your workspace code:

1. **Encryption at rest** — all `env` values are encrypted in the database.
2. **Runtime injection** — credentials are decrypted and passed to the server process only when needed.
3. **No agent exposure** — agents can *invoke* tools but cannot read or log credential values.

<Tip>
For shared workspaces, use [environment variables](/the-universal-llm-key#environment-variables) or a secrets manager (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager, Vault) and reference them in the configuration JSON via placeholder syntax (if your server supports it).
</Tip>

---

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>

<Accordion title="Server fails to initialize">
**Check**:
- The endpoint is correct and the binary/package is installed.
- Environment variables are spelled correctly and values are valid.
- The server supports MCP version 1.0 or later.
- Firewall/network rules allow outbound connections (for HTTP endpoints).
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Tools appear but agents can't invoke them">
**Possible causes**:
- The server requires credentials that weren't provided in `env`.
- The tool definition is malformed (check server logs if available).
- The agent's model doesn't support tool/function calling (use GPT-4 or Claude 3+).
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Prompt-based servers don't work">
Emergent does not yet support MCP *prompts*. If your server exposes only prompts (no tools or resources), it will not function. Check the server's documentation for a tools-based alternative.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Credentials are rejected">
- Verify the credential format (e.g., `postgresql://` vs `postgres://`).
- Ensure the credential has the necessary permissions (read/write, scopes, etc.).
- Test the credential outside Emergent (e.g., with `psql`, `curl`) to confirm validity.
</Accordion>

</AccordionGroup>

---

## Examples

### PostgreSQL database

**Endpoint:**  
```
npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres
```

**Configuration JSON:**
```json
{
  "env": {
    "DATABASE_URL": "postgresql://user:password@localhost:5432/mydb"
  }
}
```

### Git operations

**Endpoint:**  
```
uvx mcp-server-git
```

**Configuration JSON:**
```json
{
  "env": {
    "GIT_REPO_PATH": "/workspace/repo"
  },
  "args": ["--read-only"]
}
```

### Custom HTTP MCP server

**Endpoint:**  
```
https://api.example.com/mcp
```

**Configuration JSON:**
```json
{
  "env": {
    "API_KEY": "your-secret-key"
  },
  "timeout": 60000
}
```
